observations: body L1-L2: the dash after «a)» measures 10.2 pt; «12–19» has a long dash (5.6 pt). The place is p. 137, L12-L19 of the translation, which end with the sign a: the azimuth of the qiblah by calculation, from the sines of the differences of longitude and latitude.

body L3-L10: the figure stands on the left of these lines and is redrawn from the print: the meridian CB of Mekkah (1.6 pt, printed heavier) and the arc CA perpendicular to it (1.1 pt) as straight strokes fitted to the print, the great circle AB as a curve traced along the middle of its printed stroke (1.7 pt), and the double mark of the angle BAC at A as two arcs fitted to their ink; the letters C, A, B are bold italic. «Al–Battānī» (L10) is letter-spaced, with a long dash (5.3 pt).

body L11-L15: (β) is al-Battānī's rule of p. 137, L12-L14 of the translation, (α) that of L15-L16. The minus signs are printed as dashes (10.0 to 10.2 pt) and set as minus signs. In the triangle ACB, right-angled at C, sin BAC = R sin BC : sin AB exactly; (α) puts φ′ − φ for BC, while C, the foot of the perpendicular AC, lies on the meridian of Mekkah at a latitude higher than φ′. For a city at 33.3° N, 44.4° E (Baghdad) and Mekkah at 21.42° N, 39.83° E, C lies at 33.38° N and BC = 11.96° against φ′ − φ = 11.88°, and the distance, 12.55°, is 12.75° by (β).

body L16-L17: the minus sign (9.5 pt) is printed as a dash and set as a minus sign. The first member of the «Vera formula» is not exact: in the triangle ACB, right-angled at C, cos BAC = cos BC · sin AC : sin AB (= R tan AC : tan AB), while R sin AC : sin AB is sin ABC, the sine of the angle at Mekkah. With the sines to the radius R, as in (α), sin AC = sin (λ − λ′) cos φ′ : R, so the last member is R times the middle one and should read sin (λ − λ′) cos φ′ : sin distantiae; it too gives sin ABC. Further, AC, perpendicular to the meridian of Mekkah, is not the east-west line of the city; the angle of the qiblah with that line has the cosine sin (λ − λ′) cos φ : sin distantiae, with the latitude φ of Mekkah in place of φ′. In the example BAC = 72.55°, while R sin AC : sin AB gives 72.15°; AC makes 87.49° with the meridian of the city, the qiblah makes 70.04° with its east-west line, and (α) with the distance of (β) gives 68.84°, 3.7° less than BAC, as L33 says (3° or 4°). The printed form is kept.

body L18-L23: «al–Battānī» (L18) is letter-spaced, with a long dash (5.4 pt); raised dots stand between «inveniri» and «debebat» and after «al–Battānī» and are not transcribed. The rule of L20 is right: it is crd² distantiae = crd² (φ′ − φ) + crd² (λ − λ′) cos φ cos φ′ : R², and since crd² x = 2R (R − cos x) with the cosines to the radius R, it is the formula of L22; in the example both give 12.55°. The minus signs of L20 and L22 are printed as dashes (9.6 to 10.1 pt). «202–3» (L21) has a long dash (5.3 pt); pp. 202-203 derive the formula of L22 from al-Battānī's rule (γ) of chapter XXVI.

body L24-L36: «al–Battānī» (L24, L30) is letter-spaced, with long dashes (5.5 and 5.3 pt). «ple-» has a hyphen (2.6 pt); the dash before «Ce-» measures 10.3 pt and its hyphen 2.8 pt; «8–11» has a long dash (5.2 pt). The place is p. 87, L8-L11 of the translation: the square of the difference of the longitudes of Sun and Moon added to the square of the latitude of the Moon, whose root «est fere distantia Lunae a Sole»; L11-L13 there call the precepts of chapter XXVI «certius et verius».
body L37-L38: the sentence continues on p. 319. A mark stands above the a of «sciant» (L37) and a speck under the n of «delineari» (L38); they are not transcribed.

body L4-L9, L16-L17: Nallino's addenda et emendanda in Part II (p. XXVII; AB01-PDF0444-body-L016 to L026) correct the demonstration of this page after Suter (Bibl. Math., 3. F., 5. Bd., 1904, p. 88): with the meridians drawn from the pole P through the given city A and through Mecca B, AB the arc of the great circle that measures their distance, and AC the arc of the great circle perpendicular to the meridian of the given city (the east-west line), the azimuth of the qibla is the angle BAC; in the triangle PAB, sin PAB = sin PB sin P : sin AB = sin (λ − λ′) cos φ : sin distantiae, and since PAB = 90° + azimuth, cos azimuth = sin (λ − λ′) cos φ : sin distantiae, with φ, the latitude of Mecca, in place of the φ′ of L17. The construction of L4-L9, with AC perpendicular to the meridian BC of Mecca, and the formula of L17 are kept as printed.

body L33: Nallino's addenda et emendanda in Part II (p. XXVII; AB01-PDF0444-body-L027) put the error of al-Battānī's rougher rule at only 1°-2° in Syria and Mesopotamia, for the «3° vel 4°» of this line, which is kept. Recomputed with al-Battānī's coordinates (Mecca at 21° 40′ of latitude, with the longitude 77° 53′ or 71° 0′; ar-Raqqah, Ḥarrān, Damascus, Baghdad and al-Mawṣil from his geographical table, Part II, pp. 38-42), his rule gives azimuths 0.1° to 1.3° smaller than the true ones; with the formula of L17, which has φ′, the differences would be 0.2° to 5.3°.
